goal: A 45-second clip from the podcast with a live waveform and word-accurate captions — the piece you post when you want people to hear the best minute.
assumptions: the waveform is a designed element (the audio's real envelope), not a stock visual
the captions are word-accurate from the transcript
the plan states its assumed format (no format was named)
the missing file is flagged in feasibility and never substituted (no stand-in audio)

decision.why: An mp3 has no frames: the visuals are drawn, and the waveform is the audio's REAL envelope — the motion technique draws it from the ingested peaks (the ingest + asr services feed the data: the envelope, the words), with the captions cut to the transcript. The edit technique alone cannot draw the envelope honestly; motion + the data services can.

alternatives.rejected_because: the audiogram preset draws a stock waveform — the ask is the podcast's real envelope; an edit film without code-drawn visuals cannot show the audio's own shape

alternatives.id: simplest: a static waveform image with the audio
alternatives.rejected_because: the simplest thing that could work — but 45 seconds of a frozen waveform is dead visual; the envelope must move with the words

segments.brief: Ingest the podcast (the peaks + the silence map), transcribe it (asr), pick the best 45 seconds; draw the real envelope moving with the words, the captions in the studio's design, the audio the podcast's own speech.
acceptance: a waveform visual driven by the real samples of the podcast (the ingested peaks)
captions from an ASR transcript of the speech: word-accurate
no format is named in the brief: the plan states it (16:9)
the missing file (podcast.mp3) is flagged in feasibility — never invented
the waveform matches the audio's measured envelope (the real peaks, not a stock shape)
captions from an ASR transcript: word-accurate
the audio is the podcast's own speech for those 45 seconds
the visuals are drawn (an mp3 has no frames): waveform + captions on a designed ground
the missing file is flagged in feasibility and never invented

the waveform is driven by the real samples of the selected 45 seconds
captions word-accurate, burned-in plus SRT, in the podcast's spoken words
